newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific profits up from sale.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific profits up from sale.

text.p: Georgia-Pacific Corp. Thursday reported weaker first-quarter results for its pulp and paper business, but a strong market for its building products and an asset sale boosted its overall profits.

The company said net income rose to $90 million, or 99 cents a share, boosted by an after-tax gain of $80 million from the sale of its Martell, Calif., building products operation. That compared with net income of $50 million, or 55 cents, for the 1996 quarter.
Excluding the gain, the company reported operating profits of $185 million for the 1997 quarter, compared with year-ago profits of $243 million.

The Atlanta-based company said market conditions during the first quarter remained "very similar" to those of the fourth quarter of 1996. Sales for the 1997 period were $3.15 billion, compared with $3.05 billion.

"In pulp and containerboard, industry inventories increased in the quarter and prices declined," it said. "While demand for our communication papers increased, we experienced a severe decline in earnings due to lower prices than a year ago.
"The bright spot in pulp and paper continues to be our tissue business. Prices remain strong, as does profitability," it added.
The company said its lumber and gypsum operations continued to post outstanding results and plywood prices increased, while board prices remained very weak due to excess industry capacity.
"Overall, our building products manufacturing business reported operating profits more than double those of a year ago and up 25 percent from the 1996 fourth quarter," it said.
Operating profits in the building products business were $161 million, excluding the gain on the sale of the Martell assets, compared with $67 million a year ago.

"While our distribution division again reported a disappointing loss, the group is fully focused on its aggressive plan to return to profitability," it said. "This would result in a significant profit and cash flow swing in this business."
The distribution division's operating loss for the quarter was $33 million, versus a loss of $38 million a year ago that included $17 million of restructuring charges.
Georgia-Pacific's stock gained $1.25 to $72.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
